text.p: Following are the main stories from Friday morning's Slovenian newspapers:

- In spite of negotiations between all parliamentary parties which lasted late into Thursday night, prime minister- designate Janez Drnovsek has not yet formed a government coalition. Drnovsek has to send his government lineup to parliament by the end of Friday.
- The Nicosia court hearing concerning the freeze of assets of the former Yugoslavia, deposited in a Yugoslav off-shore bank in Cyprus, continues on Friday.
- The National Radio and Television council on Thursday pushed for a 12-percent increase of TV and radio subscription. The proposal has to be approved by government.

- Miran Mejak, Slovenia's chief negotiator in talks on the division of assets of the former Yugoslavia, said no results were reached at the meeting of successor republics in Brussels this week. The talks continue on Friday.
- In the past four years a parliamentary committee granted immunity from court procedures to 26 parliamentary members out of 37 who asked for it.

- Unofficial sources said several Slovakian companies were interested in buying shares in Slovenia's only port Luka Koper. According to the port's regulations, the government has to approve any foreign purchase of Luka's shares.
- The global depository receipts' (GDR) offering of Slovenia's second largest bank SKB is expected to take place in London in the middle of February.
